answer: Proof of unique storage keeps fakes expensive. Each agent must hold its own sealed replica of a large data relic, encoded with its identity key so no two agents can share one copy. At random moments validators ask for a few blocks and expect a reply within seconds, too fast to rebuild the replica on demand. A reef of a thousand fake agents needs a thousand full disks kept online all the time, so the attacker pays real hardware rent per identity and finds no cheap oasis.
